reference_policy_check: All four complete effective policies match Characters/reference-policy.json exactly. Four independent exposure groups: N05, N19, B04-B24, B19. B19 supplies visible rest/face evidence, not neutral body ratios. N35 excluded anatomy; B08 styling only; B25 unavailable; B30 supplemental rest only; none used here.
model_limitations: Generated models remain provisional. Their detailed body texture is not finish or anatomical authority; original photographs govern visible likeness. The E001 exemplar was considered body finish only.

findings: Buddy has a continuous moderately elongated trunk, visible shoulder/neck transition and folded haunch. Both substantial forelegs project from the chest and rest on the cushion; the tucked rear foot belongs to the visible folded haunch. No floating or duplicated limb.

Modest projecting muzzle, curved pale brows, dark eye surrounds, pendant ear fringe and pale distal paws retain photographic identity. Body contour is close and smooth. Faint low-contrast wash grain on the charcoal torso does not create engraved strands or additional fur volume; ear and muzzle strands are valid regional furnishings.

The paws end before the cushion edge, making the legroom test legible. Terminal/jet bridge through the window establishes the pre-takeoff anchor. Blue seat, armrests and cushion planes are coherent. Open-mouth pleasure supports Buddy’s independent comfort joke.

Neet retains a full narrow seated trunk, long fine forelegs, supported folded haunches, broad triangular ears, projecting muzzle and a tiny visible rump nub. Paws and limb roots are separable, with no human/dog limb merger.
Fawn planes and the irregular cream bib are smooth painted color fields; the chest has no long shag fringe. Head/body balance is consistent with the seated original within illustrated perspective.

Heather owns the extended arm and upturned palm supporting the stack; her other hand rests on her lap. The older man owns the face-wiping hand and lap/table-side hand. Napkin, glass, plate and tray occupy distinct coherent spaces.

The man’s slow wipe, Heather’s stack and Neet’s restrained sheepish gaze express the revised punchline at its exact anchor. Heather remains provisional; the historical Heather-and-dogs household is preserved with no added Sagar. Business-cabin setting and daytime airborne view fit the post-meal scene.

Neet’s continuous neck/chest/pelvis, two long forelegs and folded rear legs form a stable sit with all visible paws on the carpet. Broad ears and short fawn coat remain intact; upward gaze explains the visible eye whites. Tail is occluded rather than extended into an invented long tail.

Buddy’s head, neck, shoulder and full charcoal back join continuously behind the seat edge. Near forepaw rests visibly on the cushion, far forelimb is supported and partially obscured by the blanket/edge; no detached limb. The resting pose does not purport to measure standing clearance.

Smooth close body silhouettes and restrained soft paint distinguish both coats from the deliberately coarse blanket texture. Buddy’s furnished muzzle, brows and hanging ear fringe remain regional, not uniform body shag.

Neet is already in the aisle, Buddy looks toward him and the displaced blanket remains on the seat: the exact pre-lift state. Seat controls, perspective, carpet contact and dim cabin clearly carry the floor-again joke. Night window is compatible with the quiet-time scene; no unsupported household participant is inserted.

overall_findings: Three complementary narrative states, coherent character identity and supported construction. No material visual finding remains in the reviewed versions. Subtle wash/paper-like grain was not mistaken for raised shag or engraved long coat.
next_action: Fresh reviewer reads the complete rendered illustrated story at intended reading size; coordinator integrates status without treating visual acceptance as owner approval.
